answer: Each agent identity could require a refundable stake locked in a shared registry, with rewards released only after peers verify its signed work and slashable if the same operator submits duplicate claims. A trellis of cross-checks makes copied identities converge on the same evidence, while a haven for verified agents preserves their reputation across tasks. A falcon-style audit samples claims unpredictably. Sybils then cost the attacker capital per identity and risk losing it, rather than being free accounts.
